INDIAN WELLS, California, Nov 15 : Elina Svitolina said she would return to Ukraine next week after finishing runner-up at the WTA Finals on Sunday, pledging to continue supporting her country through donations, her foundation and the platform she has built in tennis. The Ukrainian lost 7-5 6-3 to Russia's Mirra Andreeva in the season-ending championship match at Indian Wells, but said the support she receives from home remains a powerful source of motivation during Russia's war in Ukraine. "It's been almost five years. I've always been supportive of the army and the soldiers," Svitolina told reporters. "They always support me by watching the matches, and I have lots of friends that are serving the country."

Svitolina, the world number six, said sport could offer people a release from the strain and uncertainty of daily life during wartime. "For me it's all about the spirit, the spirit of the people," she said. "I'm very happy that I can bring a little happiness to the people of Ukraine. "Sports in general, and in Ukraine especially, really unite people for one goal, to win." Svitolina said she had donated more than $1 million over the past five years to foundations, humanitarian assistance and initiatives run through her own charity.  Her foundation supports Ukrainian tennis players with opportunities to compete, tournament programs, travel grants and psychological assistance, she said. "If I'm not playing and if I'm with my daughter, spending quality time, I'm doing the work through my foundation," Svitolina added. The 32-year-old said Ukrainian fans had provided "incredible support" throughout the tournament, with supporters carrying flags in the stands and many following her matches overnight back in Ukraine because of the time difference. "I couldn't thank the people of Ukraine who come to watch my matches or watch at home enough," she said. Svitolina, who split up with former tennis player Gael Monfils last month, added that the visibility of Ukrainian players was helping inspire children to take up tennis and other sports, despite the difficult circumstances. "We can see a big rise in the number of kids playing tennis, trying tennis and just playing sports," she said. "It releases a lot of bad energy and a lot of tension that you are dealing with on a daily basis." She also spoke of meeting a Ukrainian refugee and aspiring player at a local high school during the event, saying the girl's determination to continue her tennis career was an example for other young Ukrainians forced to leave home.

Source: Reuters

TOKYO, Nov 16 : Japan's economy contracted by an annualised 0.1 per cent in the July-September quarter, government data showed on Monday, reflecting weak consumer spending as households grappled with elevated living costs. The first contraction in four quarters underscores the uneven nature of Japan's economic recovery, with households remaining vulnerable to persistent inflation despite rising wages. Still, the weakness is unlikely to be viewed by policymakers as a brake on Japan's moderate recovery, with resilient corporate activity, rising real wages and robust demand for artificial intelligence-related investment underpinning growth. The gross domestic product data compared with a median market forecast of 0.3 per cent annualised growth in a Reuters poll, and followed a revised 1.7 per cent expansion in the previous quarter.

The reading translated into a quarterly fall of 0.02 per cent, compared with the median estimate of a 0.1 per cent increase. Private consumption, which accounts for more than half of economic output, fell 0.3 per cent, compared with a market estimate of a 0.2 per cent decline. Household spending was hurt by persistent price pressures and poor weather, including heavy rain and typhoons during the quarter. Demand for automobiles and air conditioners retreated following the temporary boost in the previous quarter from tax and regulatory changes. Capital spending, a key driver of private demand, rose 1.6 per cent, versus a market forecast for a 1.5 per cent increase, backed by investment in labour-saving technologies and AI-related projects. Net external demand, or exports minus imports, knocked 0.6 per centage point off growth, compared with a market forecast for a 0.4 per centage point drag on GDP growth. Imports rose sharply as oil and other energy purchases recovered after Japan diversified procurement following disruptions linked to the war in the Middle East. The latest data will be closely scrutinised by the Bank of Japan as it assesses whether the economy can withstand further interest-rate increases. With stubbornly high energy costs and rising import prices from a weak yen adding to inflationary pressures, the BOJ has stepped up its policy tightening this year, delivering interest rate hikes in June and September. A monthly survey by the Japan Center for Economic Research of 37 economists showed Japan's economy is expected to grow 0.89 per cent in fiscal 2026 and 1.02 per cent in fiscal 2027, suggesting economists see growth remaining modest but resilient. Japan's longer-term growth challenges remain in focus, with the International Monetary Fund projecting the country will slip to the world's sixth-largest economy in nominal dollar terms in 2027 in dollar terms, overtaken by India and Britain. Japan is currently the world's fourth-largest after Germany.

Source: Reuters

SEOUL, Nov 16 : South Korea's SK Hynix said on Monday it plans to spend 1.4 trillion won ($1.05 billion) over the next five years to support domestic suppliers of semiconductor materials, parts and equipment, aiming to strengthen its supply chain as competition intensifies in the AI chip market. The chipmaker also outlined plans for a jointly funded 874.6 billion won testing facility at its semiconductor complex in Yongin, south of Seoul, where smaller suppliers will be able to test products under conditions similar to those on commercial chip production lines. Here are some details: • SK Hynix said its supplier support programme covers four stages - research and development, testing, mass production and sales. It aims to help smaller companies overcome financing and technology hurdles.

• The testing facility, named Trinity Fab, is a partnership between SK Hynix, the central government and local governments. It is scheduled to open in May 2027. SK Hynix will contribute 443.2 billion won, the central government 373.6 billion won and local governments 57.7 billion won, according to the company. • The facility will be housed within the first chip plant at SK Hynix's Yongin semiconductor cluster, 40 km (25 miles) south of Seoul, where the company plans to invest 600 trillion won to build four chip fabrication plants. • It will include a 3,305-square-metre (3,953-square-yard) cleanroom and equipment for processes including lithography, etching, deposition and inspection. Suppliers will be able to evaluate materials and equipment using 12-inch wafers before deploying them on production lines. • SK Hynix said the shared facility would help small suppliers reduce testing costs and shorten the time needed to bring products to market. It will be run by an independent non-profit foundation to protect intellectual property and commercially sensitive information. • Under its research support programme, SK Hynix will provide up to 50 per cent of initial development costs in advance and compensate suppliers for work undertaken even if a project fails to meet its targets. • SK Hynix and financial institutions will also provide 2 trillion won in financing backed by the Korea Trade Insurance Corporation, while other programmes offer low-interest loans and technical consulting to suppliers, including smaller subcontractors. MADRID, Nov 15 : England manager Thomas Tuchel savoured the most impressive win of his tenure as his side outplayed world champions Spain and then held on for a 3-2 win after being reduced to 10 men to win their Nations League group in Madrid on Sunday. Tuchel suffered intense criticism when England were beaten by Argentina in the World Cup semi-final this year, but the German will be justifiably lauded after his side's display against a side unbeaten in regulation or extra time in 43 matches. Had it not been for Elliot Anderson's red card for conceding the penalty that offered Spain a lifeline just past the hour mark when England led 3-0, it would have been a far more convincing scoreline. "Brilliant performance. Well deserved win. Overall we were the better team. Fantastic performance from start to finish," Tuchel, whose side were beaten 3-2 by Spain at Wembley in the Nations League in September, told ITV.

"It was a long 30 minutes (after the penalty) but I don't want to focus on that. There were so many positive things in the first 60 minutes. "Complete performance. We brought everything to the table. We were brave. Spirit wise, energy wise and also football quality was highest level. We deserved it. "We focused on our performance and attitude. I can't praise the team high enough for what they put out there. "Without the red card we were clear winners." Spain, who beat England in the Euro 2024 final and beat Argentina to win the World Cup, were left stunned as England tore them apart for an hour in the Metropolitano. They had not lost in the capital since England won there in 1987, but could have few complaints. Harry Kane opened the scoring from the penalty spot just before the break and quick-fire goals by Ezri Konsa and Ben White early in the second half confirmed England's superiority. Spain did rally, though, and but for some outstanding saves by England keeper James Trafford, they would have extended their unbeaten run. Leeds United's Trafford was surprisingly preferred to Jordan Pickford but fully justified Tuchel's decision. While Spain's proud run is over, coach Luis de la Fuente remained philosophical and said he was already looking forward to the quarter-finals in March. "England's performance today has emphasised how difficult what we've been achieving was," he said. "We have had to fight for our unbeaten run and, today, it was their day not ours - but we'll try to act the same in defeat as in victory. "Okay, we haven't often tasted defeat, but we stay proud; we stay determined - in March, we're in the quarter-finals, and we'll go to those knockouts with the intention of winning, and winning the tournament. "I'd like to be with my players again next week because if there are sad guys in my dressing room right now, then I'd like to be able to say to them over the next few days: 'Guys... be aware of the magnitude of what you've achieved, how difficult it was and how proud you should be'. "But now I have to wait until March."

Source: Reuters

Jensen Huang is considering a comeback as Nvidia 's chief executive and has discussed with confidants the possibility of returning, the Financial Times (FT) reported on Sunday (Nov 15), citing people familiar with the matter. One Huang ally told the FT they were putting together a "war room" of Silicon Valley executives to lobby for the former Nvidia chief's return and would try to garner support from the White House. "Everyone that matters in tech outside the frontier labs loves Jensen," the person said, adding that the efforts had Huang's support. T he report comes days after the FT reported that Nvidia's board had approached British chipmaker Arm Holdings CEO Rene Haas in its search for a potential successor to Jensen Huang. Nvidia did not immediately respond to a request for comment outside regular business hours. Huang stepped down on Thursday after revelations of extramarital affairs , including one involving a suspected Chinese spy that raised questions over exports of the company's advanced AI chips to China.  The scandal has plunged the chipmaker into crisis and sent shockwaves across an AI industry he helped bankroll.

Nov 15 : Intel has been sued by shareholders who accused the US chipmaker of defrauding them by concealing the impact of a prolonged slowdown in personal computer sales that caused its stock price to plunge nearly 29 per cent in a single day. In a proposed class action filed on Friday in the San Jose, California, federal court, shareholders led by a Michigan pension fund said Intel was too slow to disclose information about how slowing PC sales and an inventory glut would weigh on revenue. The shareholders said Intel's problems with PC sales and excess inventory outweighed data center construction and other benefits related to the artificial intelligence boom. They also said Intel had the motive and opportunity to defraud by raising capital in mid-August, halfway through its "disastrous" third quarter, when it sold $23 billion of stock at $95 per share.

The sale came as Intel looked to build out its chip contract manufacturing business, a key part of Chief Executive Lip-Bu Tan's business strategy. Shares of Intel closed Friday at $59.66. Intel did not immediately respond to requests for comment on Sunday. Shares of Intel fell 28.6 per cent on October 30, wiping out about $140 billion of market value, one day after the Santa Clara, California-based company projected lower-than-expected fourth-quarter revenue and profit and forecast a prolonged slowdown in PC sales. Tan told analysts that he was disappointed by manufacturing supply shortages, an "unprecedented memory crunch," and resulting softness in PCs.  "We need to address these challenges with urgency," Tan added. Like many other large technology companies, Intel has poured money into manufacturing, but supply disruptions have made it harder to benefit from growing demand for data center chips. Meanwhile, rising memory prices have made PCs more expensive, weighing on demand. Friday's lawsuit, led by the City of Southfield Fire and Police Retirement System, seeks unspecified damages for Intel shareholders between July 23, 2026, and October 29, 2026. Tan and Chief Financial Officer David Zinsner are also defendants. Intel shares are up 62 per cent this year through Friday, though they have slid from their recent peak of $142.35 on June 30.

The asphalt tanker vessel that struck a docked paddlewheel cruise boat in the Mississippi River at New Orleans last week experienced a steering problem in which its rudder was stuck in one position, United States transportation safety officials said on Sunday (Nov 15). The American Cruise Lines passenger vessel American Heritage, with 190 people aboard, capsized at the dock, though no one was killed in the collision. The Atlantic Asphalt tanker was headed upriver when it experienced a "steering casualty" in which its rudder stayed in a starboard position and the vessel veered toward the river's east bank, National Transportation Safety Board (NTSB) senior marine accident investigator Bart Barnum told a news conference in New Orleans. NTSB officials said they do not know what caused the steering problem. The tanker's voyage-data recorder was recovered on Saturday. Issues under investigation include whether the tanker's anchors were deployed and, if so, at what depth, as well as interviews with crew members and passengers, officials said. Interviews with the crew of the Atlantic Asphalt are scheduled over the next week, they said. Harbour personnel, firefighters and onlookers scrambled to pull passengers from the cruise vessel to safety after the collision. The cruise vessel toppled over into the river.

INDIAN WELLS, California, Nov 15 : Russian teenager Mirra Andreeva beat Ukraine's Elina Svitolina 7-5 6-3 on Sunday to win the WTA Finals, completing an unbeaten singles debut at the season-ending championships in Indian Wells without dropping a set. Andreeva threw her racket into the air and jumped for joy when Svitolina put an overhead into the net on match point, before hugging coach Conchita Martinez and her team. "I'm super thankful to my team for helping me work hard every day and pushing me to my limits," she said during the trophy ceremony. "Thanks for fighting with me." The 19-year-old French Open champion won all five of her matches at the event, which brings together the top eight players of the season.

She takes home the maximum prize money of $3.37 million and the Billie Jean King Trophy. King watched the final from the stands on a sunny day in the California desert. MIRRA IN THE DRIVER'S SEAT Andreeva will rise to a career-high world number two in Monday's rankings and will move within 300 points of Elena Rybakina. She also won a custom Mercedes-Benz AMG SL 55 painted in the WTA's signature purple, though she does not yet have a driver's licence. "This is an amazing motivation for me to get my driver's licence as fast as I can," she said during the trophy ceremony. "But I still want to just try to give it a little spin, maybe a couple of metres. I'm sure I'm going to be able to do that or at least honk a little bit. "If not, then look, I have five people on my team. I'm gonna be a passenger princess forever so that's also an option for me." TENSE BATTLE Andreeva was the favourite against Svitolina, the 2018 champion, and had beaten her 6-4 6-0 on Monday in the round-robin stage. The first set was tight, with long rallies as both players tried to control points by pushing the other from side to side and drawing them in off the baseline. Andreeva served for the set at 5-4 but struggled, hitting two double faults and a backhand long to let Svitolina back into it. She stayed composed, though, breaking Svitolina in the next game and then showing great poise to serve out the 55-minute set. The intensity stayed high in the second set, including a 10-minute seventh game, the longest of the tournament, which featured six deuces. Svitolina won the game when Andreeva sent a backhand wide to cut her opponent's lead to 4-3.  But frustration began to mount for Svitolina during the subsequent changeover as she gestured to her team and Andreeva rolled on from there, easily holding serve and then breaking Svitolina for a sixth time to seal the win. SVITOLINA THANKS UKRAINIAN FANS Svitolina, 32, said she hoped her return to the highest level after becoming a mother would inspire other women and athletes. "I'm really happy to be in great form and to be coming back after pregnancy. Hopefully it inspires some ladies and athletes around the world to believe that it's possible," she said. Svitolina did not shake hands with Andreeva after the match, maintaining her policy of not doing so with Russian or Belarusian opponents following Russia's 2022 invasion of Ukraine, which Moscow launched using Belarus as a staging ground. She also did not acknowledge Andreeva during the trophy ceremony. "I want to say thank you also to people in Ukraine for supporting me and being on this journey with me," she said. The eight-day, $10 million tournament was moved from Riyadh to Indian Wells Tennis Garden due to the US-Israeli war on Iran. The event will move to Charlotte, North Carolina, next year.

Source: Reuters

MADRID, Nov 15 : England ended world champions Spain's record unbeaten run with a 3-2 win in Madrid to top their Nations League group, but Italy's hopes of joining them in next year's quarter-finals were dashed as they lost 4-1 in Belgium on Sunday. Captain Harry Kane's penalty shortly before the interval and second-half goals by Ezri Konsa and Ben White meant England became the first team to beat Spain in regulation or extra time since Colombia in March 2024, although their run of 43 games without defeat included a penalty shootout loss to Portugal. Spain finally came alive after England's Elliot Anderson conceded a penalty for hauling back Lamine Yamal and was sent off in the 63rd minute, allowing Mikel Oyarzabal to reduce the arrears from the spot. Substitute Nico Williams then made it 3-2 but England survived a late siege to secure a statement victory.

England lost the reverse fixture 3-2 at home to Spain at Wembley but their impressive away win in the Metropolitano Stadium means both teams end on 15 points in Group A3, with Thomas Tuchel's England topping the standings on goal difference. Spain could have few complaints as they were second best for much of the game although they also progress to the quarter-finals as runners-up. "We knew we were going to beat them tonight. The message from the manager after the Croatia game has been so positive," England midfielder Declan Rice said. "The first 10 minutes was the best we've played. Pressure, pressure. It's a massive win." ITALY CRASH OUT IN BRUSSELS Italy went into their clash in Brussels top of Group A1 after their 3-1 win against France on Thursday but came crashing back to earth as they were comfortably beaten by Belgium. Francesco Pio Esposito gave Italy an early lead but their joy was short-lived as Belgium scored three times before the interval through Maxim De Cuyper, Nathan Ngoy and Jeremy Doku. Diego Moreira added a fourth for Belgium after the break. France beat Turkey 2-1 in Bordeaux thanks to an own goal by Emirhan Topcu and an effort by Eli Junior Kroupi, meaning they won the group with 13 points, ahead of Belgium who ended on 12. Italy, on 10 points, missed out. The other match in Group A3 saw Croatia beat the Czech Republic 2-1. England's 10th successive away victory was arguably their best result under Tuchel's reign. They dominated the first half against strangely lacklustre opponents and got their noses in front when Ballon d'Or winner Kane was brought down in the penalty area by Pau Cubarsi and then calmly dispatched his kick past Unai Simon for his 93rd goal for his country. Konsa was completely unmarked to head England's second in the 53rd minute from Rice's corner and when Arsenal team mate White fired a low shot past Simon to make it 3-0 four minutes later, the visitors were in dreamland. Everything changed though when Oyarzabal beat James Trafford from the penalty spot after Anderson's rash decision. Yamal set up Williams in the 75th minute and England were forced to defend desperately late on with Trafford making a stunning double save to keep his side in front. The draw for the Nations League quarter-finals takes place next week but Italy will not be in it. Manager Roberto Mancini had no complaints though as his side collapsed against Belgium despite taking the lead. "They were the better side; we struggled too much physically and in one-on-one situations. Despite a good start, they were simply better," Mancini said. "We paid a physical price,—we were clearly feeling some fatigue from the match against France." The quarter-final line-up will be confirmed after Group A2 concludes on Monday with Germany needing to beat the Netherlands in Berlin while Greece, who are second, face Serbia. In Group A4, which concludes on Tuesday, Portugal have qualified with runners-up spot between Denmark and Norway who face each other in Copenhagen.

Source: Reuters

Nov 15 : The United States and Canada will meet again in the women's ice hockey world championship final, after both sides comfortably won their semi-finals in Herning, Denmark on Sunday. The Americans scored three times in 95 seconds to seal a 5-0 win over Finland in Sunday's first semi-final. The defending champions will play for a 12th title in their 25th consecutive final. Canada advanced with a comfortable 3-0 win over Sweden. Sarah Fillier opened the scoring on a power play before Sarah Wozniewicz doubled the lead, and Emma Maltais added a third early in the final period. Sweden will face Finland for bronze. Finland had early chances to open the scoring against the United States, but goals from Kelly Pannek and Alex Carpenter sent the Americans into the first intermission two goals ahead.

The United States have reached every final since the tournament began in 1990 and have won the title 11 times. They have faced Canada in every final except in 2019, when the Americans beat hosts Finland in a shootout. Canada, however, lead the all-time standings with 13 world titles. "We expected a good fight from them. Finland is a fast team, they're skilled, and they're relentless the whole sixty," Harvey said. "We're hoping to carry the momentum into tomorrow, build on the good habits, and win a gold medal," she added. "They were better in every area of the game but we gave our all, too bad we couldn't score on our chances. We put up a fight and I'm proud of our team," said Finland's Emma Nuutinen. BROWNSVILLE, Texas, Nov 15 : A Vulcan rocket owned by United Launch Alliance, the joint venture of Boeing and Lockheed Martin, failed on Sunday shortly after liftoff from Florida, destroying its payload of 40 satellites for Amazon's Leo internet network in the launch company's first mission failure. The rocket failed roughly 10 minutes after liftoff from the Cape Canaveral Space Force Station in Florida, and the cause was not immediately clear. It represented a major setback for the two-decade-old company's new flagship rocket as it sought to begin a regular cadence of launches for Amazon's burgeoning satellite internet constellation. "Based on data received by our Launch Director, we confirm that the Vulcan vehicle launched from Space Launch Complex 41 suffered an anomaly 10 minutes into the flight and failed to deliver the Amazon mission to orbit," ULA said in a statement. "Every flight generates data, and every flight teaches us something. Since the anomaly just occurred, we don’t have any specific data yet to understand what occurred today."

The mission was Vulcan's fifth since its 2024 debut and first in nine months, following a launch hiatus drawn out by separate technical investigations into its solid rocket side-boosters and its core BE-4 engines, which are supplied by Amazon founder Jeff Bezos' Blue Origin space company. The boosters were being scrutinized for issues encountered on Vulcan's last two flights, including a mission in February for the US Space Force. Both missions successfully delivered their payloads to orbit, but the Pentagon had not yet approved the rocket to resume flying national security payloads, pending its performance with the Amazon mission on Sunday. Blue Origin's New Glenn rocket with the BE-4 engine had a launchpad explosion in May, and its investigation determined the engine was the cause. That led the company to modify those delivered to ULA for Vulcan, ULA spokesperson Jessica Rye told Reuters in August. It was unclear if the BE-4 engines played a role in Sunday's mission failure. It appeared to occur after the separation of Vulcan's second stage, the portion carrying the Amazon satellites, from the first-stage booster powered by the BE-4 engines. The failure is another setback for Amazon as it races to deploy satellites using third-party launch providers, many of which have had groundings and failures. The New Glenn explosion in May happened days before it was due to launch Amazon Leo satellites. The rocket failures have persistently held up Amazon's bid to rival SpaceX's vast Starlink internet network, which has more than 11,000 satellites and millions of customers worldwide. Since 2025, 398 Leo satellites have been deployed across 14 launches, about 12 per cent of Amazon's plan. The company has hoped to start initial internet service this year.

Source: Reuters
